meaning.name: Send a parcel
meaning.purpose: The integrator's program, with an order to send, ends with the parcel delivered and every move of it told to the shop.
meaning.steps: 1. The integrator starts with a test key: its shipments are never collected and its labels say TEST. A5, R11 2. The shop's program registers the shipment with the sender, the recipient, the parcel and the service; one over a limit is refused with the field and why, and is sent again. A1, R1 3. A key that lacks the scope is refused with the scope it lacks: the shop's site, whose key may only read, registers nothing. A1, R6 4. The shop's program produces the label, and the warehouse prints the A6 PDF and sticks it on the parcel; the subscribers hear labelled. A5, A10, R2, R8 5. Called off before the courier has it, the shipment is cancelled, its label void; once collected, the cancel is refused. A6, R3 6. The parcel is handed to the courier, and the depot feed moves the shipment, collected, in transit, out for delivery; each move is told to the subscribers. A10, R8 7. The shop's site asks for the shipment's events and shows them to its customer. A4, R4 8. The shop's program finds a shipment again by its order's reference, among its shipments newest first. A2, R5 9. The parcel is delivered, or returned after three attempts or a refusal. A10, R8
meaning.user: the integrator, through the shop's program

meaning.goes wrong: | What fails | Then | Seen by | Stands on | |---|---|---|---| | the subscriber answers other than 2xx, or nothing within ten seconds | the delivery is tried again five times, after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 6 hours, then dropped, R9 | the subscriber, by X-Parcelpost-Attempt above 1; Parcelpost's log, a line for each failed try | R9 | | ten tries in a row fail | the subscription is paused, and what happens while it is paused is never sent, R9 | the integrator, in the list of subscriptions, A8: not active, with its failures; the account's technical contact, by email, R10 | A8, R9, R10 | | the signature does not match at the subscriber | the subscriber refuses the delivery, and Parcelpost counts the refusal as a failed try, R9 | the subscriber's own log | R9 | | the subscription was stopped | nothing more is sent to it, R7 | the integrator, who no longer finds it in the list, A8 | R7, A8 |
meaning.name: Tell a subscriber of a move
meaning.purpose: Parcelpost, when a shipment's status changes, ends with each subscriber that asked for it told once, or the subscription paused.
meaning.steps: 1. Parcelpost finds each subscription of the shipment's account that is active and asked for shipment.status.changed. A10, R8 2. It sends each one delivery: the shipment's id, reference, status and service and its last event, signed with the subscription's secret. A10, R8 3. The subscriber checks the signature and answers 2xx within ten seconds; the delivery counts, and the failures in a row are none again. A10, R8 4. Otherwise the try failed, and the delivery is tried again after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 6 hours, then dropped. A10, R9 5. At the tenth failed try in a row, the subscription is paused and sent nothing more, and the account's technical contact is emailed that day. R9, R10 6. The integrator sees it not active in the list of subscriptions, stops it and subscribes again. A8, A9, A7, R7

meaning.name: Keep the webhooks
meaning.purpose: The integrator, with a server that takes deliveries, ends with a subscription that is active and a secret kept where the server checks signatures with it.
meaning.steps: 1. The integrator subscribes an https address to shipment.status.changed, shipment.delivery.attempted, or both; an http address or an event Parcelpost does not send is refused. A7, R7 2. The integrator keeps the secret the answer holds, since it is never shown again, and the server checks each delivery's signature with it. A7, R7, R8 3. The integrator lists the subscriptions, each with whether it is active and its failures in a row. A8, R7 4. A paused subscription is stopped, and the address subscribed again, with a new secret; a paused one cannot be resumed. A9, A7, R7, R12

meaning.name: Register a shipment
meaning.statement: When an integrator registers a shipment with a service, a sender, a recipient and a parcel within the limits, Parcelpost shall make it, created, with an id of PP and twelve digits, and answer it with the address of its tracking page.

meaning.says: Given a key with shipments:write, when a standard shipment of a parcel of 1.2 kg, 40 by 30 by 10 cm, to Leipzig, DE, is registered, then the answer is 201 with an id of PP and twelve digits and the status created.
Given a recipient in the US, when the shipment is registered, then the answer is 422, says that Parcelpost does not deliver to US, and names recipient.country.
Given a parcel of 30 kg, when it is registered, then it is made; given one of 31 kg, the answer is 422 and no shipment is made.

Given a parcel of 120 by 50 by 40 cm, a girth of 300 cm, when it is registered, then it is made; given one of 120 by 50 by 41 cm, the answer is 422 and says the girth is 302 cm and 300 cm is the most.
Given the service economy and a parcel of 25 kg, when it is registered, then the answer is 422, names service and says to choose standard.
Given a key without shipments:write, when a shipment is registered, then the answer is 403 and names shipments:write.

meaning.name: Tell the account when a subscription is paused
meaning.statement: When a subscription is paused, Parcelpost shall send an email to the account's technical contact the same day, saying that the subscription is paused.

meaning.says: Given a subscription paused at 14:10, when it is paused, then the account's technical contact receives an email that day saying that it is paused.
Given a subscription that fails nine tries in a row and then delivers, when the tenth try counts, then no email is sent.

meaning.name: A test key's shipments are never collected
meaning.statement: Where a key is a test key, Parcelpost shall mark the labels of its shipments TEST, say so in the label's answer, and never have its shipments collected.

meaning.says: Given a test key, when a label is produced with it, then the answer says test is true and the PDF says TEST.
Given a live key, when a label is produced with it, then the answer says test is false.
Given a labelled shipment of a test key, when a week passes, then it is still labelled.

meaning.name: Resume a paused subscription
meaning.statement: When an integrator resumes a paused subscription, Parcelpost shall make it active again and send what follows.

meaning.name: Produce the label
meaning.statement: When an integrator asks for the label of a shipment that is not cancelled, Parcelpost shall answer the address of its A6 PDF with the barcode, the same label every time it is asked for.

meaning.says: Given a created shipment, when its label is asked for, then the answer holds the address of an A6 PDF, the shipment is labelled, and its events end with Label produced.
Given a labelled shipment, when its label is asked for again, then the same address is answered and no event is added.
Given a cancelled shipment, when its label is asked for, then the answer is 409, says that the shipment is cancelled and has no label, and no label is made.
Given a key without the scope labels, when a label is asked for, then the answer is 403 and names labels.

meaning.name: Cancel a shipment before collection
meaning.statement: When an integrator cancels a shipment the courier does not yet have, Parcelpost shall mark it cancelled, so that its label is void, and tell the subscribers.

meaning.says: Given a created shipment, when it is cancelled, then the answer is 204 and its events end with Cancelled by the sender.
Given a labelled shipment, when it is cancelled, then it is cancelled, and its label asked for afterwards is refused with 409.
Given a collected shipment, when it is cancelled, then the answer is 409, says that it is collected and that only one not yet collected can be cancelled, and it stays collected.
Given a cancelled shipment, when it is cancelled again, then the answer is 409 and nothing changes.
Given a subscription to shipment.status.changed, when a shipment of its account is cancelled, then one delivery says cancelled.

meaning.name: Follow a shipment
meaning.statement: When a program asks for a shipment or its events, Parcelpost shall answer the shipment's status as it stands and every event it has, oldest first, each with its time, its kind, its place and its text.

meaning.says: Given a labelled shipment, when its events are asked for, then two are answered, Shipment registered and Label produced, in that order, and the status is labelled.
Given a shipment the depot feed has scanned at a depot, when its events are asked for, then the scan is among them with its place, and the status is as it was before the scan.
Given a key with shipments:read alone, when a shipment of its account is asked for, then it is answered.
Given an id no shipment has, when it is asked for, then the answer is 404 and says that no shipment has that id.

meaning.name: List the shipments
meaning.statement: When a program lists its account's shipments, Parcelpost shall answer them newest first, fifty to a page, with how many there are in all, kept to a status and to the sender's reference where the call names them.

meaning.says: Given an account with 120 shipments, when page 3 is asked for, then the 20 oldest are answered and the total is 120.
Given three shipments with the reference VL-1047, when the list is asked for with that reference, then those three are answered and no other.
Given the status labelled, when the list is asked for with it, then only labelled shipments are answered.
Given an account with no shipments, when the list is asked for, then no item is answered and the total is 0.
Given a key without shipments:read, when the list is asked for, then the answer is 403.

meaning.name: A key does only what its scopes allow
meaning.statement: If a call comes with no key, with a key that is not known, with a key that lacks the scope the call needs, or names another account's shipment or subscription, then Parcelpost shall refuse it: 401 for the key, 403 naming the scope, and 404 for what is not the account's.

meaning.says: Given a call with no Authorization header, when it is made, then the answer is 401 and says to send Authorization: Bearer and the key.
Given a revoked key, when any call is made with it, then the answer is 401 and says the key is not known or has been revoked.
Given a key with shipments:read alone, when it registers a shipment, then the answer is 403 and says the key lacks the scope shipments:write.
Given a shipment of another account, when its id is asked for, then the answer is 404, as for an id no shipment has.
Given a subscription of another account, when it is stopped, then the answer is 404 and it is not stopped.

meaning.name: Subscribe to the events
meaning.statement: When an integrator subscribes an https address to one or both of the events Parcelpost sends, Parcelpost shall keep the subscription, active, and answer the secret that signs its deliveries, this once.

meaning.says: Given a key with the scope webhooks, when an https address is subscribed to shipment.status.changed, then the answer is 201 with an id of WH and eight hexadecimal characters, the address, the event, the secret, and active.
Given an address that starts with http://, when it is subscribed, then the answer is 422 and no subscription is made.
Given the event shipment.picked.up, when it is subscribed to, then the answer is 422 and says there is no such event.
Given an account's subscriptions, when they are listed, then each is answered with its address, its events, whether it is active and its failures in a row, and none with its secret.
Given a subscription, when it is stopped, then the answer is 204 and it is listed no more.
Given a key without the scope webhooks, when a subscription is made, listed or stopped, then the answer is 403 and names webhooks.

meaning.name: Send each event, signed
meaning.statement: When a shipment's status changes, or the courier tries to deliver it and cannot, Parcelpost shall send that event to each active subscription of the shipment's account that asked for it, one delivery each, signed with the subscription's secret.

meaning.says: Given an active subscription to shipment.status.changed, when a shipment's first label is produced, then one POST arrives with the header X-Parcelpost-Event shipment.status.changed, X-Parcelpost-Attempt 1, and a body that says labelled.
Given that delivery, when the subscriber computes the HMAC SHA-256 of the body with its secret, then it equals X-Parcelpost-Signature after sha256=.
Given any delivery, when its body is read, then it holds the shipment's id, reference, status and service and its last event, and no address of the sender or the recipient.
Given a subscription to shipment.delivery.attempted alone, when a label is produced, then nothing is sent to it.
Given a subscription of another account, when this account's shipment changes status, then nothing is sent to it.
Given a shipment just registered, when it is made, then nothing is sent: registering is not a change of status.

meaning.name: Try again, and pause a subscription that keeps failing
meaning.statement: If a subscriber does not answer a delivery with 2xx within ten seconds, then Parcelpost shall try it again after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 6 hours, drop it after that, and pause the subscription at its tenth failed try in a row.

meaning.says: Given a subscriber that answers 500, when a delivery is sent, then it is tried again 1 minute later with X-Parcelpost-Attempt 2.
Given a subscriber that answers nothing within ten seconds, when a delivery is sent, then the try counts as failed.
Given a delivery whose sixth try fails, when it fails, then it is not tried again.
Given a subscription with nine failed tries in a row, when the tenth fails, then it is listed as not active with 10 failures, is sent nothing more, and what happens while it is paused is never sent.
Given a subscription with nine failed tries in a row, when the next try is answered 204, then its failures in a row are 0 and it stays active.

meaning.assumptions: - The integrators' tickets about missed webhooks are tagged the same way after the rebuild as before. To check: count the tags of the first quarter after the move against the tickets read by hand. - The onboarding log records the day a key is given and the day of the first label with a live key, as it does today. To check: ask the onboarding team for the first five integrators of 2027.
meaning.journey: 1. The integrator gets a test key and registers a shipment with it; a parcel over a limit is refused, one field at a time. 2. With a live key, the shop registers a shipment for each order and produces its label, which the warehouse prints and sticks on the parcel. 3. The parcel is handed to the courier; from then on the depot feed moves the shipment, collected, in transit, out for delivery, delivered or returned. 4. The integrator's server hears of each move by webhook and updates the order; the shop's site shows the tracking to the customer. 5. Today this is where it goes wrong: the integrator's server fails ten tries in a row, the subscription is paused, and nothing more arrives until someone notices. 6. While the parcel is not yet collected, the shop may cancel the shipment, and its label is void.
meaning.name: Parcelpost
meaning.non-goals: - Resuming a paused subscription through the API: the integrator stops it and subscribes again, which the brief says is enough for the rebuild, R12 (E8). - Returns: they are booked with the depot by phone, and a shipment the courier has cannot be cancelled here (E10). - Pages of any kind: the shops show the tracking on their own sites (E10, E92). - Parcels over 30 kg: that is freight, not Parcelpost (E10). - How the depot feed moves a shipment once it is collected: the depots own it, and this API only answers what it has moved (E92).
meaning.problem: The API is being rebuilt, and nothing a shop's program sends or receives is to change; without a specification the new team would read the old code and guess. Today integrators lose the moves of their shipments without knowing it: 23 of the 140 tickets from integrators in the third quarter of 2026 were about webhooks never received, most of them from a subscription paused after ten failures that nobody had noticed (E2). Before the fix of August 2026, 9 labels were produced for shipments already cancelled, and the parcels reached a depot with no shipment behind them (E3). A new integrator takes a median of 6 working days from their key to their first label with a live key, by the onboarding log, most of it spent meeting the limits one refusal at a time (E4).
meaning.release plan: | Release | Holds | Outcome | |---|---|---| | First | R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8, R9, R11 | the API as it runs today, on the new platform: a shop registers, labels, follows and cancels its shipments, and hears of each move | | Later | R10 | the account hears the same day that a subscription was paused |
meaning.summary: Parcelpost is the API a shop calls to send parcels: it registers a shipment, produces its label, answers where the parcel is, cancels it while it can be, and tells the shop of every move by webhook. This specification says what the API does today, call by call and event by event, so that the team rebuilding it on the courier's new platform in the first half of 2027 builds the same API, and the shops that call it notice nothing (E1).
meaning.users: The integrator: the developer at a shop or an agency who connects the shop to Parcelpost, holds the key with every scope, registers the shipments, produces the labels and subscribes to the events (U1). The shop's site: the shop's own pages, which show the tracking to its customers with a key that may only read (U2). The depot feed: the courier's depots, whose scans move each shipment once the parcel is handed over; it is a system, and it calls nothing described here (U3).
